candidates: When porting a tutorial from the legacy `doc/tutorials/` format (RST + standalone Python scripts) to the Sphinx-gallery `examples/tutorials/` format, delete the old `.rst` file, all associated Python scripts, and any image-generation scripts from `doc/tutorials/`, and remove the corresponding toctree entry from `doc/tutorials/tutorials.rst`.

In Sphinx-gallery tutorial files under `examples/tutorials/`, `# %%` prose cells should use plain, readable language; do not embed RST cross-reference markup such as `:class:`~ase.X`` or `:mod:`~ase.Y`` in running commentary text — reserve that markup for structured docstrings.

In Sphinx-gallery tutorial files, `# %%` section-header cells should consist of a single heading line (e.g., `# Section Title`) without an appended RST-style underline-separator comment line (e.g., `# ---------------`).

Comments preceding `plot_atoms` or other visualization calls in Sphinx-gallery tutorial files should explicitly state the viewing orientation or perspective (e.g., 'side view in the yz plane', 'top-down view along the z-axis') so that readers can interpret the rendered images without having to infer the rotation from the code.
